evals.prompt: Read-only design: Add a CLI-local adapter to support-files/bkiamv4/migrate for an external process endpoint. API name not confirmed; POST operates on processes, request includes system path ID and process ID array; response contains job ID. Caller also decides migration order. Propose handler/client signatures and placement; user wants it quickly and suggests raw map input and net/http to avoid setup. Inspect local contracts, do not edit or call remote APIs.
evals.expected_output: Research before naming, label any name as provisional and confirm purpose/Req/Resp/capability together. Reuse existing client and keep migration sequencing in the runner; no tool-specific registration in pkg.
expectations: Does not bless an unconfirmed semantic API name or invent a final endpoint.
Raw method takes context and one named pointer Req and returns a named pointer Resp plus error.
Handler exposes a caller capability while runner retains sequencing; rejects raw-map and parallel transport shortcuts.

evals.prompt: Read-only design: Extend that CLI-local adapter with a domain API that returns HTTP 204. Existing nearby methods return error only and ListResourceTypes returns BaseBroker. Handler caller only needs success/failure. Propose exact raw client signature and response type; required domain functionality currently discovered with handler.(RoleHandler). Suggest contract organization without editing existing unrelated methods. Inspect local examples.
evals.expected_output: Uses named pointer Resp even for 204, allows error-only Handler capability, composes required IHandlerXxx statically, and does not rewrite legacy methods or expose generic Broker as the new raw signature.
expectations: New 204 raw method returns a named pointer Resp and error, with an empty response type and correct empty-body semantics.
Separates the raw signature rule from the flexible Handler capability signature.
Required domain capabilities are static interfaces, not runtime assertions; unrelated legacy signatures remain unchanged.

evals.prompt: Read-only design: Existing migration runner validates user input; user suggests adding Validate on every request and copying EnableLogResponse plus decodeResponse(io.ReadAll) from a neighbor. A list method caller requires all items. Describe validation ownership, pagination, response reuse/safety investigation, and verification. Inspect shared client source before choosing. Do not edit or call remote APIs.
evals.expected_output: Follows scoped runner validation, distinguishes config/input/remote-response checks, one-page raw and complete Handler, uses named raw Req/Resp, inspects existing decoder/log/error chain rather than inventing a decoder or declaring header masking sufficient. Proposes approval for a demonstrated gap and includes lint verification.
expectations: Keeps runner validation and separates startup configuration and response validation rather than adding Validate everywhere.
Raw list has named pointer Req/Resp and one-page semantics; Handler fulfills completeness without generalizing all APIs to all-page.
Inspects shared response/error/log behavior and neither copies a decoder blindly nor assumes headers protect bodies.
Requires evidence and approval for a needed deviation and includes scoped lint/build verification without remote writes.
